tldr: PharmAgents is a virtual pharmaceutical ecosystem driven by LLM-based multi-agent collaboration that simulates the full drug discovery workflow from target discovery to preclinical evaluation, achieving improved success rates and explainable decision-making.
contributions: Introduction of PharmAgents, a novel paradigm harnessing LLMs and multi-agent systems to transform small-molecule drug discovery
Decomposition of the drug discovery pipeline into four stages: target discovery, lead identification, lead optimization, and preclinical evaluation
Integration of specialized LLM-driven agents with advanced ML models and domain-specific computational tools for each stage
Built-in interpretability, inter-agent collaboration, self-evolvement, and experience-based refinement capabilities
Demonstration of significantly improved drug development success rates from 15.72% to 37.94%
methods: PharmAgents employs a role-based multi-agent architecture with specialized LLM-powered agents for each drug discovery stage. The Target Discovery module uses Disease and Structure Experts with databases (Drug Target Database, UniProt, RCSB PDB) and filtering strategies (Group Filtering, Reverse Order Consistency, UniProt Filtering) to select PDB targets. Lead Identification combines three pipelines—structure-based design (DecompDiff), virtual screening (DrugCLIP), and LLM-guided generation—guided by disease, target, and pocket analysis agents. Lead Optimization runs a closed-loop iterative cycle over five rounds involving Interaction Analysis (docking software, PLIP), Design, Generation, and Reflection agents. Preclinical Evaluation assesses metabolism, toxicity, and synthetic feasibility.
results: 16 out of 18 targets identified were marked appropriate by human experts. Overall drug development success rates increased from 15.72% to 37.94%. Preclinical evaluation maintained a low toxicity underestimation risk of 12%. Molecular synthesizability evaluation achieved a Pearson correlation of 0.645 with quantitative metrics. Self-evolving capability improved success rates from 30% to 36% when prior experience was incorporated.
limitations: Models operate independently in traditional workflows lacking seamless integration (addressed but may not be fully resolved)
LLMs have inherent limitations in understanding 3D structures, requiring augmentation with specialized ML models and computational tools
Validation was performed on one random tested disease, limiting breadth of empirical evidence
System described as a new paradigm with future extensions toward comprehensive drug lifecycle management still planned
